answer:
The R21/Matrix-M vaccine has shown high efficacy in clinical trials, though reported figures vary by trial and setting. One summary states that R21/Matrix-M was well tolerated and offered high efficacy against clinical malaria in African children [1]. Another source notes that its reported efficacy and immunogenicity have varied across clinical trials conducted in different populations and settings [3].

According to a perspective paper, the vaccine demonstrated remarkable efficacy, reaching 77% effectiveness in Phase 2 clinical trials [5]. In Phase 3 trials, the 12-month vaccine efficacy was 75% in locations characterized by seasonal variations and 68% in standard locations [5]. Against multiple clinical malaria episodes, the efficacy was 75% at the seasonal sites and 67% at the standard sites [5]. The same source also says the vaccine offers up to 77% protection against the malaria parasite in clinical trials [5]. Two other sources describe R21/Matrix-M as supported by field-efficacy and immunogenicity evidence, but their snippets do not give specific efficacy numbers [2][6].
